description: Given the root of a binary tree, return all root-to-leaf paths in any order. A leaf is a node with no children. Each path should be represented as a string with nodes separated by "->".
intuition: Think of each root-to-leaf path as a journey. DFS naturally explores one complete path at a time. By building the path string as you go deeper and recording it when you hit a leaf, you capture every possible journey through the tree.
approach: Use DFS traversal. At each node, append its value to the current path. When a leaf is reached, add the complete path string to the results. Backtrack by removing the node after exploring its subtrees.
explanation:
1. Start DFS from the root with an empty path list.
2. At each node, append its value as a string to the path.
3. If the node is a leaf (no children), join the path with "->" and add to results.
4. Otherwise, recurse on left and right children.
5. Pop the current node from the path when backtracking.
hints: A leaf node has no left or right child.
Use DFS and build the path string as you go deeper.
Remember to backtrack (remove the current node) after exploring subtrees.
